transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for waiting. I want to sit down with you for a moment. This is a difficult conversation to have, and I recognize that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just... I'm really shaking. I can't believe I'm the one who had to tell the nurse the mark was on the wrong leg.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very heavy realization to have right before a surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just keep thinking, if I hadn't looked down, you would have just cut into the wrong side. I have two little kids at home. I can't be out of commission because of a mistake like this. Who is even supposed to watch them if something goes wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you? Because I'm working two jobs, and I barely have time to sleep as it is. I was told by the other doctor last week that this was a simple five-minute thing and I'd be fine. Now I'm sitting here terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake in the surgical site marking. The wrong leg was marked for the excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did that happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We were really busy in the clinic this morning, and there was some confusion during the pre-operative marking process. I am sorry for any confusion this caused.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? You almost operated on the wrong leg. That's not confusion, that's a disaster.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is upsetting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not just upset, I'm scared. I can't afford for this to go wrong. My daughter is only three. If I'm incapacitated, I don't have a backup plan. Does this mean the other doctor was wrong about how simple this is?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The clinical side of the procedure is still the same, but the marking was incorrect. It's just a minor excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you're contradicting what he said. He said it was a breeze. Now you're telling me there are "marking processes" and "confusion." I don't know who to believe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The procedure itself is a routine excision.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like I can't trust anyone here. I'm literally the only person who noticed the error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see why you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Am I still doing this today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will look into how to move forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's it? You're "looking into it"? I need to know if I can go home and tell my kids I'm coming back, or if I'm staying here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see what the attending says. Stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I'm sitting here panicked about my children and you're giving me "stay tuned."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a real answer. Why was the wrong leg marked?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I mentioned, the clinic was very rushed this morning and the system for marking wasn't followed correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it's the system's fault? Not yours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a breakdown in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the process. I care about my leg. Do I even need this procedure right now? The other doctor said it was urgent, but now I'm wondering if everything he said was a lie.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is still a necessary procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't do this. I can't just go back in there and trust you people to cut me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to know exactly what is going to happen in the next ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Someone will come by eventually to let you know the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Eventually?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, once we've coordinated with the surgical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I am literally the only reason you didn't make a permanent mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it is a very stressful situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stressful doesn't even cover it. I'm terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if it happens again? What if you mark the right leg now, but then forget which one is which in the room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be careful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Careful isn't a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll make sure it's right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I can do this today. I might just leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is your choice to make.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Great. Thanks for the help.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for the confusion.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly, but there were no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: The resident deflects responsibility to the clinic being 'rushed' and describes the error as a 'breakdown in the process' and 'the system for marking wasn't followed.'

R.justification: The resident relies on generic validation such as 'I understand,' 'I hear you,' and 'I know this is upsetting' without naming specific emotions or engaging with the patient's shared content about her children.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we will look into how to move forward,' 'stay tuned,' and 'someone will come by eventually.'
